title: Balanced Binary Tree
statement: Return true when the tree is height-balanced. A tree is height-balanced when the depths of the two subtrees of every node differ by at most 1.
hints: A naive check recomputes height at every node and is quadratic.
Return the height, and use a sentinel such as -1 when a subtree is already unbalanced.
A node is balanced when both children are balanced and their heights differ by at most 1.

approaches.name: Height at every node
approaches.explanation: Simple and easy to overshoot the time limit.

editorial: If either child returns -1, propagate -1. If the absolute difference of the two heights exceeds 1, return -1. Otherwise return 1 + the larger height. The tree is balanced when the root's call does not return -1.

examples.explanation: The left spine is too deep.
